description: How a metadata column name maps to a level of the experimental hierarchy. The single most consequential judgement in a perturbation audit is which column is the experimental unit, and it is usually made implicitly by whatever the analysis groups by. Making it explicit is what lets a wrong denominator be caught instead of inherited.

observation_unit.role: What was measured. Never a biological replicate on its own.

assignment_unit.role: What the perturbation was assigned to. Bounds a within-screen contrast; does not stand in for a population.

technical_process_unit.role: A processing split. Replicating it replicates the protocol, not the biology.

screen_process_unit.role: One execution of the screen. Bounds scope; several screens of the same line are still one biological source.

biological_replicate_candidate.role: The only level that can carry a population claim, and only when it is crossed with the perturbation rather than confounded with it.

condition_or_time.role: The contrast axis. Confounding this with a replicate level is the classic fatal design error.

unclassified_role: A column nothing matches is not benign — it is a level nobody has thought about. It is reported, never silently dropped.
